plane 2, artifacts B.bundle (15 pages) + the wasmtime ELF (11137 pages)

13 of 13 acceptance items from the independent review, ALL evidenced from the file rather than from a
success code - the thirteenth was inferred in the first run and this one records the bytes:
  reclaim succeeds (rax_out=0x0)                       status: admitted=0x00 AND key=0
  whoami refused 0x80001003                            report refused 0x80001003
  the slot reads as ZEROS                              the slot is writable again
  thaw ALLOWED on a reclaimed frame, then re-validates second reclaim is a coded no-op (0x8000100c)
  re-stage resets the length (59829)                   re-admit both kinds
  named again (ce52712f...)                            report GRANTED after the full cycle

THE POST-CYCLE REPORT, CHECKED FROM ITS BYTES (the first run recorded only the SVSM's success code, so its
binding, level and app ID were an inference about the mechanism rather than evidence of it):
  report_data[0:32]  = Bind2(the RE-registered key, nonce, RuntimeID)   recomputed by runtime.mjs, equal
  report_data[32:64] = ce52712f... from the measured table
  vmpl               = 2
  measurement        = the igvmmeasure digest above
  and against the first report: the re-registered key is byte-identical, so report_data is IDENTICAL across the
  reclaim cycle, while the two reports are NOT the same bytes - a fresh PSP signature over the same claim.

A LIMIT OF THIS RUN, for the monitor port's acceptance later: the registered key is the deterministic stand-in
(i*11+5), not a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, and the SVSM treats it as opaque bytes. So this exercises the mechanism
but NOT end-to-end recomputation from a real TLS handshake; that run must register a domtls-minted key.

The SVSM's own log for the cycle:
  plane 2 admitted kind 0, 15 pages frozen read-only to every guest plane
  plane 2 admitted kind 1, 11137 pages frozen read-only to every guest plane
  plane 2 reclaimed: 11152 pages zeroed and unfrozen, key and naming forgotten
  plane 2 admitted kind 0/1 again

WHAT THIS IS NOT. This is the half of the lifecycle a plane performs AT ITS OWN REQUEST. It is not plane teardown:
VMSAs, every page the plane owns beyond its artifacts, the calling area and the secrets copy are untouched, and a
